panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: Axial T2 MRI shows bilateral hypothalamic T2 hyperintensity in a 14-year-old boy with tuberculous meningitis; the caption provides a specific manifestation, but no controlled vocabulary finding matches it. b: Diffusion-weighted MRI shows restricted diffusion in the right thalamus, globus pallidus, and lateral putamen, consistent with tuberculous vasculitic infarct. c: ADC map confirms restricted diffusion corresponding to the acute infarct in the basal ganglia/thalamus described in the caption. d: Follow-up axial T2 MRI at 15 days shows dilated lateral ventricles consistent with hydrocephalus and periventricular/corona radiata T2 hyperintensity in tuberculous meningitis.
